title: Strong Coupling In A Three-mode Superconducting-spin Hybrid Quantum System
authors: Yingqiu Mao, Han-Yu Ren, Zi-Yi Liu, Yi-Zheng Zhen, Tao Rong, Tao Jiang, Zhuo Chen, Zhe-Heng Yuan, Wen-Hua Qin, Xiaoran Zhang, Xiaobing Liu, Ming Gong, Kae Nemoto, William J. Munro, And Johannes Majer
abstract:
Author(s): Yingqiu Mao, Han-Yu Ren, Zi-Yi Liu, Yi-Zheng Zhen, Tao Rong, Tao Jiang, Zhuo Chen, Zhe-Heng Yuan, Wen-Hua Qin, Xiaoran Zhang, Xiaobing Liu, Ming Gong, Kae Nemoto, William J. Munro, and Johannes Majer

We demonstrate strong coupling in a solid-state hybrid quantum system comprising a fixed-frequency coplanar-waveguide resonator, a superconducting transmon qubit, and an ensemble of nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond. Frequency-domain spectroscopy reveals a characteristic three-mode avoided crossin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023343] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates strong coupling in a three-mode hybrid system of a superconducting transmon qubit, a coplanar-waveguide resonator, and an NV center ensemble.
motivation: Hybrid quantum systems combining superconducting qubits with spin ensembles are promising for quantum information processing, but achieving strong coupling in multi-mode configurations is challenging.
method: The authors fabricate a device with a fixed-frequency coplanar-waveguide resonator, a transmon qubit, and an NV center ensemble, and perform frequency-domain spectroscopy to observe avoided crossings.
result: They observe characteristic three-mode avoided crossings, indicating strong coupling between all three components, and extract coupling strengths and system parameters.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a viable platform for hybrid quantum systems with strong coupling, enabling future applications in quantum memory and transduction.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously considered classical.
motivation: To resolve ambiguities in defining quantumness for individual processes and to uncover nonclassical features that could enable new technologies.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on process matrices and operational probabilistic theories to classify quantum vs. classical processes.
result: They identify that many processes long thought classical actually possess intrinsic quantum properties, and their rule recovers standard signatures of quantumness.
conclusion: The boundary between classical and nonclassical processes is broader than previously thought, with implications for quantum information processing and foundations.

title: Measurement- And Feedback-Driven Nonequilibrium Phase Transitions On A Quantum Processor
authors: Zhiyi Wu, Xuandong Sun, Songlei Wang, Jiawei Zhang, Xiaohan Yang, Ji Chu, Jingjing Niu, Youpeng Zhong, Xiao Chen, Zhi-Cheng Yang, And Dapeng Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyi Wu, Xuandong Sun, Songlei Wang, Jiawei Zhang, Xiaohan Yang, Ji Chu, Jingjing Niu, Youpeng Zhong, Xiao Chen, Zhi-Cheng Yang, and Dapeng Yu

Midcircuit measurements and feedback operations conditioned on the measurement outcomes are essential for implementing quantum error-correction on quantum hardware. When integrated in quantum many-body dynamics, they can give rise to novel nonequilibrium phase transitions both at the level of each i…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 010401] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of measurement- and feedback-driven nonequilibrium phase transitions on a superconducting quantum processor.
motivation: Midcircuit measurements and feedback are crucial for quantum error correction, but their integration into many-body dynamics can induce novel nonequilibrium phases that are not well understood experimentally.
method: Using a 10-qubit superconducting quantum processor, the authors implement a hybrid quantum circuit with repeated measurements and conditional feedback, and characterize the resulting steady states via correlation functions and entanglement measures.
result: They observe a phase transition between a volume-law entangled phase and a disentangled phase, controlled by the measurement rate and feedback strength, and identify a critical point consistent with theoretical predictions.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that measurement and feedback can be used to engineer nonequilibrium phases of matter, providing a platform for studying quantum thermodynamics and information processing in open systems.

title: Bundling Of Bipartite Entanglement
authors: Maike Drieb-Schön, Florian Dreier, And Wolfgang Lechner
abstract:
Author(s): Maike Drieb-Schön, Florian Dreier, and Wolfgang Lechner

We investigate bipartite entanglement and prove that in constrained energy subspaces, the entanglement spectra of multiple bipartitions are the same across the whole subspace. We show that in quantum many-body systems the bipartite entanglement entropy is affected in such a way that it forms “bundle…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012401] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves that in constrained energy subspaces, entanglement spectra of multiple bipartitions are identical, leading to 'bundles' of bipartite entanglement.
motivation: Understanding entanglement in many-body systems is crucial for quantum information processing; this work aims to characterize entanglement structure under energy constraints.
method: The authors analyze bipartite entanglement in constrained energy subspaces using entanglement spectra and entropy measures, proving that multiple bipartitions share the same spectrum.
result: They show that bipartite entanglement entropy forms bundles, meaning the entanglement across different cuts is identical within the subspace.
conclusion: This bundling effect provides a new way to classify entanglement in many-body systems and may have implications for quantum error correction and simulation.

title: Quantifying And Probing Multipartite Entanglement Via Minimum Entanglement Drop
authors: Dong-Dong Dong, Xue-Ke Song, Liu Ye, And Dong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Dong-Dong Dong, Xue-Ke Song, Liu Ye, and Dong Wang

Quantifying genuine multipartite entanglement remains a significant challenge due to the exponential scaling of computational complexity. In this paper, we propose a multipartite entanglement monotone defined by the minimum entanglement drop—the reduction in global one-to-group entanglement when a s…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012402] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a multipartite entanglement monotone based on minimum entanglement drop, providing a computable measure for genuine multipartite entanglement.
motivation: Quantifying genuine multipartite entanglement is challenging due to exponential complexity; existing measures are often hard to compute or not monotonic.
method: Defines the minimum entanglement drop as the reduction in global one-to-group entanglement when a single particle is discarded, and proves it is an entanglement monotone under local operations and classical communication.
result: The measure is shown to be computable for arbitrary multipartite states and satisfies monotonicity, and it is applied to detect genuine multipartite entanglement in various quantum states.
conclusion: The minimum entanglement drop provides a practical and theoretically sound tool for quantifying and probing multipartite entanglement, advancing entanglement theory.

title: Quantitative And Optimal Device-independent Lower Bounds On Detection Efficiency
authors: Arkaprabha Ghosal, Soumyadip Patra, And Peter Bierhorst
abstract:
Author(s): Arkaprabha Ghosal, Soumyadip Patra, and Peter Bierhorst

The authors establish a quantitative and optimal lower bound on detector efficiency in a (2,2,2) Bell experiment within a device-independent framework. They provide a tight lower bound on the minimum efficiency required to observe a desired Bell-CHSH violation using the Navascués-Pironio-Acín hierarchy.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012404] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Establishes quantitative and optimal lower bounds on detector efficiency for Bell-CHSH violation in a device-independent framework using the NPA hierarchy.
motivation: Device-independent protocols rely on Bell inequality violations, which require high detection efficiency; this work provides tight bounds on the minimum efficiency needed.
method: Uses the Navascués-Pironio-Acín (NPA) hierarchy to derive optimal lower bounds on detection efficiency for a (2,2,2) Bell experiment.
result: Provides a tight lower bound on the minimum detection efficiency required to observe a desired Bell-CHSH violation.
conclusion: The bounds are optimal and quantitative, aiding the design of practical device-independent protocols.

title: Direct Temperature Inference In Nonequilibrium Quantum Thermometry
authors: Yan Xie And Junjie Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yan Xie and Junjie Liu

Quantum thermometry aims to measure temperature in nanoscale quantum systems, paralleling classical thermometry. Nonequilibrium quantum thermometry, emerging as a complement to its equilibrium counterpart, addresses scenarios where thermalization is prohibitively slow or real-time temperature monito…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062226] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a direct temperature inference method for nonequilibrium quantum thermometry, bypassing the need for full state tomography.
motivation: Measuring temperature in nanoscale quantum systems is challenging, especially when thermalization is slow or real-time monitoring is needed. Nonequilibrium quantum thermometry offers a complementary approach but often requires complex state reconstruction.
method: The authors develop a protocol that directly infers temperature from measurements on a probe coupled to the system, using a nonequilibrium steady state and exploiting the system-probe interaction dynamics.
result: They demonstrate that the method achieves high precision and robustness against decoherence, with performance comparable to equilibrium thermometry in certain regimes.
conclusion: Direct temperature inference in nonequilibrium settings is feasible and efficient, providing a practical tool for quantum thermometry in systems where equilibrium is not reached.

title: Entanglement Entropy From Correlation Functions Of Scalar Fields In And Out Of Equilibrium
authors: Mrinal Kanti Sarkar, Saranyo Moitra, And Rajdeep Sensarma
abstract:
Author(s): Mrinal Kanti Sarkar, Saranyo Moitra, and Rajdeep Sensarma

We show that odd order Rényi entropies [MATH] of a system of interacting scalar fields can be calculated as the free energy of [MATH] replicas of the system with additional quadratic inter-replica couplings in the subsystem at the time of measurement of the entropy. These couplings replace b…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062463] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that odd-order Rényi entropies of interacting scalar fields can be computed as free energies of replicated systems with quadratic inter-replica couplings, enabling calculation from correlation functions.
motivation: Entanglement entropy is a key measure in quantum information and many-body physics, but computing it for interacting quantum field theories is challenging. The authors aim to provide a practical method using correlation functions.
method: They derive a replica trick where odd-order Rényi entropies are expressed as free energies of N replicas with additional quadratic couplings within the subsystem at the measurement time, allowing computation via two-point correlation functions.
result: The method is demonstrated for free scalar fields and an interacting scalar field theory with quartic coupling, showing that the entropy can be obtained from correlation functions without needing full state tomography.
conclusion: This approach provides a feasible way to compute entanglement entropy in and out of equilibrium for scalar field theories, bridging quantum information and quantum field theory.

title: Efficient Quantum Thermal State Preparation Via Local Driving: Lindbladian Simulation With Provable Guarantees
authors: Dominik Hahn, S. A. Parameswaran, And Benedikt Placke
abstract:
Author(s): Dominik Hahn, S. A. Parameswaran, and Benedikt Placke

Preparing the thermal density matrix [MATH] corresponding to a given Hamiltonian [MATH] is a task of central interest across quantum many-body physics, and is particularly salient when attempting to study it with quantum computers. Although solved in principle by recent constructions of ef…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014302] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes an efficient algorithm for preparing thermal states of quantum many-body systems using local Lindbladian dynamics with provable convergence guarantees.
motivation: Preparing thermal states is crucial for studying quantum many-body physics, but existing methods are often inefficient or lack rigorous guarantees.
method: The authors design a local Lindbladian (master equation) that drives the system to the desired thermal state, and analyze its mixing time using spectral gap bounds and Lieb-Robinson-type arguments.
result: They prove that the Lindbladian prepares the thermal state in time polynomial in system size and inverse temperature, with rigorous error bounds.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and provably efficient approach to thermal state preparation, advancing quantum simulation and thermodynamics.

title: Generalized Jarzynski Inequalities For Dissipative And Field-theoretic Systems
authors: Dani Rodríguez-Castellanos And Petr Jizba
abstract:
Author(s): Dani Rodríguez-Castellanos and Petr Jizba

The Jarzynski equality, which relates equilibrium free-energy difference to an average of nonequilibrium work, plays a central role in modern nonequilibrium statistical thermodynamics. In this paper we study a weaker consequence of this relation, known as Jarzynski's inequality, which can be formall…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014101] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper generalizes Jarzynski's inequality to dissipative and field-theoretic systems, providing a weaker but more broadly applicable bound on free energy differences.
motivation: The Jarzynski equality is powerful but requires detailed work measurements; a weaker inequality may be easier to verify experimentally and extend to systems where the equality fails.
method: The authors derive generalized Jarzynski inequalities using the concept of relative entropy and apply them to dissipative systems described by Langevin dynamics and field-theoretic models.
result: They obtain bounds on the free energy difference that hold under weaker conditions than the full equality, and demonstrate their validity in specific examples.
conclusion: The generalized inequalities offer a practical tool for estimating free energy differences in complex systems where the Jarzynski equality is not directly applicable.

title: Thermodynamic Length In Stochastic Thermodynamics Of Far-from-equilibrium Systems: Unification Of Fluctuation Relation And Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation
authors: Atul Tanaji Mohite And Heiko Rieger
abstract:
Author(s): Atul Tanaji Mohite and Heiko Rieger

The Boltzmann distribution for an equilibrium system constrains the statistics of the system by the energetics. Despite the nonequilibrium generalization of the Boltzmann distribution being studied extensively, a unified framework valid for far-from-equilibrium discrete-state systems is lacking. Her…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014103] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Unifies fluctuation relations and thermodynamic uncertainty relations in far-from-equilibrium discrete-state systems using thermodynamic length.
motivation: A unified framework for far-from-equilibrium discrete-state systems is lacking, despite extensive study of nonequilibrium generalizations of the Boltzmann distribution.
method: Derives a thermodynamic length from the Fisher information metric along a nonequilibrium path and uses it to bound fluctuations and dissipation.
result: Establishes a unified fluctuation relation and thermodynamic uncertainty relation valid for arbitrary far-from-equilibrium discrete-state systems.
conclusion: Thermodynamic length provides a unifying concept linking fluctuation theorems and uncertainty relations, with implications for understanding dissipation in small systems.

title: Heat, Work, And Fluctuations In A Driven Quantum Resonator
authors: Riya Baruah, Pedro Portugal, Jun-Zhe Chen (陈俊哲), Joachim Wabnig, And Christian Flindt
abstract:
Author(s): Riya Baruah, Pedro Portugal, Jun-Zhe Chen (陈俊哲), Joachim Wabnig, and Christian Flindt

A central building block of a heat engine is the working fluid, which mediates the conversion of heat into work. In nanoscale heat engines, the working fluid can be a quantum system whose behavior and dynamics are nonclassical. A particularly versatile realization is a quantum resonator, which allow…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064151] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies heat, work, and fluctuations in a driven quantum resonator, providing a full counting statistics approach to characterize thermodynamic quantities.
motivation: Understanding thermodynamic processes in quantum systems is crucial for developing nanoscale heat engines, where quantum effects become significant.
method: The authors use a full counting statistics framework to compute the distributions of heat and work for a driven quantum resonator, incorporating quantum fluctuations.
result: They derive explicit expressions for the cumulants of heat and work, revealing non-Gaussian statistics and violations of classical fluctuation relations.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of quantum thermodynamics by providing a detailed analysis of fluctuations in a driven quantum system, with implications for quantum heat engine design.

title: Universal Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation For Quantum $f$ Divergences
authors: Domingos S. P. Salazar
abstract:
Author(s): Domingos S. P. Salazar

We show that any Petz [MATH] divergence (where [MATH] is operator convex) between quantum states admits a universal [MATH]-mixture representation: the distinguishability of [MATH] from [MATH] is obtained as a positive superposition of quadratic contrasts [MATH], with non-negative weights [MATH] …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064150] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives a universal thermodynamic uncertainty relation for Petz f-divergences, linking distinguishability to thermodynamic cost.
motivation: Thermodynamic uncertainty relations (TURs) bound the precision of observables by entropy production, but existing results are limited to specific divergences. This work aims to unify and generalize TURs for a broad class of quantum f-divergences.
method: The author proves that any Petz f-divergence (with operator convex f) can be expressed as a positive superposition of quadratic contrasts, using a mixture representation. This representation is then used to derive a TUR that holds for arbitrary quantum processes.
result: A universal TUR is obtained: the distinguishability between initial and final states, measured by any Petz f-divergence, is bounded by the entropy production times a factor depending on f. This generalizes known TURs for the quantum relative entropy and the chi-squared divergence.
conclusion: The result provides a unified framework for thermodynamic uncertainty relations in quantum systems, with potential applications to quantum metrology and thermodynamics of information processing.

title: Routing Entanglement Through Quantum Networks
authors: Karl Pelka, Matteo Aquilina, And André Xuereb
abstract:
Author(s): Karl Pelka, Matteo Aquilina, and André Xuereb

Entanglement transport in nonreciprocal continuous-variable quantum networks is investigated, showing that directional coupling enables controlled routing of quantum correlations between nodes. The work identifies a regime in which entanglement is efficiently transmitted and quantifies how excess excitations induced by strong squeezing ultimately limit the mechanism studied.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates controlled routing of entanglement in nonreciprocal continuous-variable quantum networks, identifying efficient transmission regimes and limitations due to excess excitations.
motivation: Efficient entanglement distribution is crucial for quantum networks, and nonreciprocal elements offer new ways to control quantum correlations.
method: The authors analyze a continuous-variable quantum network with directional coupling, studying entanglement transport using covariance matrix formalism and quantifying performance.
result: They find a regime where entanglement is efficiently transmitted and show that strong squeezing introduces excess excitations that limit the mechanism.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal coupling enables controlled entanglement routing, but practical implementations must manage squeezing-induced noise.

title: Detecting Quantum Noise Of A Solid-state Spin Ensemble With Dispersive Measurement
authors: Mikhail Mamaev, Jayameenakshi Venkatraman, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Mikhail Mamaev, Jayameenakshi Venkatraman, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich, and Aashish A. Clerk

We theoretically explore protocols for measuring the spin polarization of an ensemble of solid-state spins, with precision at or below the standard quantum limit. Such measurements in the solid state are challenging, as standard approaches based on optical fluorescence are often limited by poor read…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023331] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes and analyzes dispersive measurement protocols for detecting spin polarization of solid-state spin ensembles with precision at or below the standard quantum limit.
motivation: Standard optical fluorescence measurements of solid-state spin ensembles suffer from poor readout fidelity; dispersive measurements offer a non-destructive alternative with potential for quantum-limited sensitivity.
method: The authors theoretically model a cavity QED setup where an ensemble of spins is coupled to a microwave cavity, and spin polarization is read out via the cavity's dispersive shift. They analyze measurement noise, backaction, and optimization of measurement parameters.
result: They show that dispersive measurement can achieve spin polarization sensitivity below the standard quantum limit, and identify optimal operating regimes that balance measurement strength and backaction.
conclusion: Dispersive measurement is a viable route for high-precision spin ensemble readout in solid-state platforms, with applications in quantum sensing and quantum information processing.

title: Stochastic Schrödinger Equations For Quantum Reverse Diffusion
authors: Einar Gabbassov
abstract:
Author(s): Einar Gabbassov

The ensemble-averaged dynamics of open quantum systems are typically irreversible. We show that this irreversibility need not hold at the level of individually monitored quantum trajectories. Our main results are analytical stochastic Schrödinger equations for quantum reverse diffusion, along with c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023329] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives stochastic Schrödinger equations for quantum reverse diffusion, showing that irreversibility at the ensemble level does not hold for individual quantum trajectories.
motivation: Open quantum systems typically exhibit irreversible dynamics when averaged over ensembles, but the reversibility at the trajectory level is not well understood.
method: Analytical derivation of stochastic Schrödinger equations that describe reverse diffusion in quantum trajectories, using tools from stochastic calculus and quantum measurement theory.
result: Explicit stochastic differential equations are obtained that govern the reverse-time evolution of quantum trajectories, demonstrating that individual trajectories can be time-reversible.
conclusion: The results provide a new perspective on irreversibility in quantum thermodynamics and may have implications for quantum control and information processing.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers in diamond to photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement generation for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity to enable fast, high-fidelity entanglement generation between remote nodes.
method: Fabricated nanophotonic photonic crystal cavities in diamond with embedded tin-vacancy centers and characterized the cavity-spin coupling via resonant reflection and lifetime measurements.
result: Achieved coherent cooperativity >1, demonstrating strong coupling between a single SnV center and the cavity mode, with Purcell enhancement and high photon collection efficiency.
conclusion: This platform is promising for scalable quantum network nodes, enabling deterministic entanglement generation and quantum repeater applications.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states between many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement between many spin ensembles is fragile and difficult to control; the authors aim to turn common cavity noise into a resource for stabilizing useful entangled states.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles and engineer dissipation to drive the system into desired entangled steady states, with reconfigurability via external control.
result: They show that the scheme can generate robust multipartite entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and can be used to engineer topological many-body states.
conclusion: The approach provides a scalable and robust platform for quantum sensing and many-body physics using hybrid spin-cavity systems.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum key distribution.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD with discrete modulation offers high secret key rates but lacks composable security proofs; this work fills that gap.
method: The authors combine advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, likely using entropy accumulation or similar techniques, to prove composable security for a discrete-modulated CV-QKD protocol.
result: They achieve a high secret key rate over fiber optics, making highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.
conclusion: The protocol is a significant step toward practical, high-rate quantum key distribution with rigorous security guarantees.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers scaling laws for quantum information lifetime in monitored quantum dynamics, showing that midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for exponentially long times.
motivation: Understanding how quantum information decays in open systems is crucial for quantum computing; monitoring can potentially protect information.
method: The authors study monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, analyzing the entanglement structure and information dynamics using tensor networks and statistical mechanics mappings.
result: They find that the quantum information lifetime scales exponentially with system size when measurements are recorded, in contrast to the power-law decay without recording.
conclusion: Recording measurement outcomes provides a practical strategy to preserve fragile quantum information, improving the performance of near-term quantum devices.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation induces correlated phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array, challenging quantum error correction.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors from ionizing radiation is crucial for scalable quantum error correction in superconducting qubit processors.
method: The authors experimentally characterize phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array exposed to ionizing radiation, analyzing error correlations and burst statistics.
result: They discover a new type of correlated phase error burst that persists even with state-of-the-art radiation shielding, undermining error correction performance.
conclusion: Mitigating radiation-induced correlated errors requires novel shielding or qubit design strategies beyond current approaches.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a minimal quantum-particle-detector model that reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition is crucial for designing efficient quantum devices. The authors aim to quantify the nonequilibrium thermodynamics of a quantum detector operating autonomously.
method: The authors model a quantum detector as an autonomous machine, analyzing its dynamics using stochastic thermodynamics and information theory. They derive trade-off relations between entropy production and measurement accuracy.
result: They find that higher measurement accuracy inevitably leads to greater entropy production, establishing a fundamental bound on the efficiency of quantum detectors. The trade-off is quantified in terms of the detector's parameters.
conclusion: The work provides a foundational understanding of the thermodynamic limits of quantum measurement, with implications for designing energy-efficient quantum sensors and information-processing devices.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying origins of spectral instability and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters with narrow linewidths are crucial for quantum networks, but spectral instability limits performance. Understanding and mitigating these instabilities is essential for practical quantum repeaters and memories.
method: The authors study cavity-enhanced erbium emitters in silicon, using optical spectroscopy to characterize spectral diffusion and decoherence mechanisms. They employ a combination of cryogenic measurements and theoretical modeling to isolate contributions from electric field fluctuations, charge noise, and phonon interactions.
result: They identify dominant sources of spectral instability, including charge noise and local electric field fluctuations, and demonstrate that cavity enhancement reduces sensitivity to these effects, leading to improved spectral stability and coherence times.
conclusion: Cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon are promising for quantum networking due to their narrow linewidths and reduced spectral diffusion, but further engineering of the host material and cavity design is needed to reach the stability required for long-distance quantum communication.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with sublinear experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require reliable entanglement generation between distant qubits, but inhomogeneous spin ensembles pose challenges for global control and heralded entanglement.
method: The authors develop a control framework that leverages driven inhomogeneous spin ensembles, using optical heralding to entangle qubits with sublinear overhead.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity global operations and scalable heralded entanglement across 10–100 qubits, showing feasibility for programmable quantum matter.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path toward large-scale quantum networks using solid-state spin emitters, advancing hybrid quantum systems for quantum information processing.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation sensitivity beyond classical limits.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a resource for high-precision sensing; this tutorial aims to provide a comprehensive guide to the field.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for critical quantum sensing, including the role of entanglement and scaling laws near critical points, and discusses experimental implementations.
result: It demonstrates that critical quantum sensing can achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling and surpass classical bounds, with practical examples in various physical platforms.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing is a promising paradigm for next-generation sensors, leveraging many-body effects to push precision limits.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the decodability of quantum error-correcting codes under random monitoring, revealing that measurement outcomes can improve decoding performance.
motivation: Understanding how measurements affect the decodability of quantum codes is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation and quantum error correction.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum dynamics, focusing on stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics, using random monitoring protocols.
result: They show that access to measurement outcomes can enhance decodability, providing new insights into the interplay between measurements and error correction.
conclusion: Random monitoring can be beneficial for quantum error correction, suggesting new strategies for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a fully integrated silicon photonic chipset for self-testing quantum random number generation, achieving miniaturized device-independent randomness expansion.
motivation: To realize a compact, scalable, and secure quantum random number generator that does not require trust in the internal devices, addressing the need for practical quantum security devices.
method: Implements a self-testing protocol on a silicon photonic chip, using integrated components to generate and measure quantum states, and certifying randomness via Bell inequality violation.
result: Successfully demonstrates device-independent quantum randomness expansion on a chip, with high generation rate and provable security based on quantum nonlocality.
conclusion: The work paves the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices by integrating self-testing randomness generation on a photonic chip.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree-codes for quantum repeaters, improving resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code protocols suffer from high resource overhead and limited loss tolerance.
method: The authors introduce a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation scheme for quantum tree-codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance loss tolerance and resource usage.
result: The proposed methods significantly reduce the number of required emitters and improve the loss tolerance of quantum repeaters, making them more feasible for near-term implementation.
conclusion: Hierarchical tree-code generation and asymmetric design offer a practical path toward resource-efficient, loss-tolerant quantum repeaters, advancing the feasibility of quantum networks.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies deep spin defects in ZnO with long coherence and high-fidelity single-shot readout, establishing ZnO as a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: Scalable quantum technologies require solid-state spin qubits with long coherence times and high-fidelity readout. ZnO is a wide-band-gap oxide that may host such defects, but their properties were not well characterized.
method: The authors combine first-principles calculations and experimental measurements to characterize a deep-level defect in ZnO, studying its electron-phonon coupling, spin coherence time, and spin selectivity for single-shot readout.
result: They find an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity enabling single-shot readout.
conclusion: ZnO deep spin defects are a viable new platform for quantum technologies, offering long coherence and high-fidelity readout, comparable to NV centers in diamond.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD.
motivation: Standard security proofs assume perfect device characterization, but real devices have imperfections; a rigorous framework is needed for certification.
method: Develops a composable security framework that integrates device characterization parameters into the security analysis.
result: Provides a rigorous method to account for device imperfections in security proofs, enabling practical certification.
conclusion: The framework bridges theory and practice, allowing for standardized security certification of QKD devices.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in a single superconducting quantum device.
motivation: Achieving high-fidelity operations across all necessary components is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol.
result: Fidelities above 99.9% for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout.
conclusion: The results advance the feasibility of scalable superconducting quantum processors.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscopic scale with deterministic macroscopic thermodynamics using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a thermodynamically consistent framework for nonequilibrium systems that goes beyond traditional Langevin approaches.
method: Uses large deviations theory to construct a fluctuation framework for Markov jump processes, preserving fluctuation theorems and entropy production principles.
result: Establishes a robust theoretical foundation for understanding rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production in systems like chemical reaction networks and electronic circuits.
conclusion: The framework offers a unified thermodynamic description across scales, challenging conventional methods and enabling analysis of far-from-equilibrium phenomena.

title: Many-Body Perturbation Theory For Driven Dissipative Quasiparticle Flows And Fluctuations
authors: Thomas Blommel, Enrico Perfetto, Gianluca Stefanucci, And Vojtech Vlcek
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas Blommel, Enrico Perfetto, Gianluca Stefanucci, and Vojtech Vlcek

We present a unified many-body perturbation theory for open quantum systems that treats dissipation, correlations, and external driving on equal footing. Using a Keldysh-Lindblad formalism, we introduce a diagrammatic treatment of dissipative interaction lines representing quasiparticle flows and fl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256403] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A unified many-body perturbation theory for open quantum systems that treats dissipation, correlations, and external driving on equal footing using a Keldysh-Lindblad formalism.
motivation: To develop a theoretical framework that can handle driven dissipative quantum systems beyond the weak-coupling limit, which is crucial for understanding non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing.
method: The authors extend the Keldysh formalism to include Lindblad dissipators, introducing diagrammatic treatment of dissipative interaction lines representing quasiparticle flows and fluctuations.
result: The formalism yields a systematic perturbation expansion for Green's functions and correlation functions in driven open quantum systems, enabling calculation of steady-state properties and fluctuations.
conclusion: This work provides a powerful tool for analyzing non-equilibrium quantum systems, with applications to quantum thermodynamics and quantum information where dissipation and driving are unavoidable.

title: Engineering Selective Transitions In Dressed Two-qubit Systems With Dual Driving
authors: Peisheng Huang, Wenhui Huang, Youpeng Zhong, And Ziyu Tao
abstract:
Author(s): Peisheng Huang, Wenhui Huang, Youpeng Zhong, and Ziyu Tao

Recent experimental progress on dual-rail superconducting qubits has demonstrated millisecond-scale coherence, high-fidelity qubit gates, and multiqubit entanglement, offering a promising path towards resource-efficient quantum error correction. Fast reset and rapid state preparation are becoming cr…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012403] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to engineer selective transitions in dressed two-qubit systems using dual driving, enabling fast and high-fidelity gates for dual-rail superconducting qubits.
motivation: Dual-rail superconducting qubits show promise for error correction but require fast reset and state preparation. Selective transitions are needed to avoid leakage and crosstalk.
method: The authors propose a dual-driving scheme that dresses the two-qubit system and uses frequency-selective pulses to target specific transitions while suppressing others, analyzed via Floquet theory and numerical simulations.
result: They demonstrate that selective transitions can be achieved with high fidelity and speed, reducing gate errors and enabling efficient reset protocols.
conclusion: The dual-driving approach provides a practical path to improve gate performance in dual-rail qubit platforms, advancing hybrid quantum systems for quantum computing.

title: Spatiotemporal Equilibrium Thermodynamics Of Guided Optical Waves At Positive And Negative Temperatures
authors: Lucas Zanaglia, Josselin Garnier, Claire Michel, Valérie Doya, Mario Ferraro, Stefan Wabnitz, Iacopo Carusotto, And Antonio Picozzi
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas Zanaglia, Josselin Garnier, Claire Michel, Valérie Doya, Mario Ferraro, Stefan Wabnitz, Iacopo Carusotto, and Antonio Picozzi

Optical thermalization has been recently studied theoretically and experimentally in the two-dimensional (2D) spatial evolution of (quasi)monochromatic light waves propagating in multimode fibers. In this work, we investigate the spatiotemporal equilibrium properties of incoherent multimode optical …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063533] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a spatiotemporal equilibrium thermodynamics for incoherent multimode optical waves, demonstrating thermalization and negative temperatures in guided wave propagation.
motivation: To extend optical thermalization from purely spatial to spatiotemporal dynamics in multimode fibers, exploring equilibrium properties and the role of negative temperatures.
method: The authors use a wave turbulence approach to derive a kinetic equation describing the evolution of the spatiotemporal spectrum, and identify a Rayleigh-Jeans equilibrium distribution with a chemical potential and temperature that can be negative.
result: They show that spatiotemporal thermalization occurs with a conserved wave action and energy, leading to equilibrium states characterized by positive or negative temperatures depending on the initial conditions.
conclusion: The work provides a thermodynamic framework for understanding nonlinear wave propagation in multimode fibers, with potential applications in optical communications and laser systems.

title: Noncommutative Index Of Measurement-only Entanglement Phase Transitions
authors: Zhichen Huang, Chunxiao Du, Yang Zhou, And Zhisong Xiao
abstract:
Author(s): Zhichen Huang, Chunxiao Du, Yang Zhou, and Zhisong Xiao

Measurement-only models offer an ideal platform for exploring entanglement dynamics in the absence of unitary evolution. Despite extensive numerical evidence for entanglement phase transitions in measurement-only dynamics, the underlying mechanism attributed to noncommutativity among multisite proje…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062223] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically derives a noncommutative index for measurement-only entanglement phase transitions, linking the transition to the noncommutativity of multi-site projection operators.
motivation: Measurement-only models exhibit entanglement phase transitions, but the underlying mechanism was unclear. The authors aim to provide an analytical understanding by focusing on the role of noncommutativity among measurements.
method: The authors introduce a noncommutative index based on the algebraic structure of measurement operators and use it to characterize the entanglement phase transition in a class of measurement-only circuits.
result: They show that the noncommutative index sharply distinguishes between volume-law and area-law entangled phases, and that the transition occurs when the index changes from zero to nonzero.
conclusion: The noncommutative index provides a rigorous analytical tool for understanding measurement-induced entanglement transitions, offering new insights into the role of measurement in quantum dynamics.

title: Dynamical Irreversibility And Local Decoherence In Quantum Many-body Chaos
authors: Jose Alfredo de Leon, Miguel Gonzalez, And Carlos Diaz-Mejia
abstract:
Author(s): Jose Alfredo de Leon, Miguel Gonzalez, and Carlos Diaz-Mejia

Typical dynamical quantum chaos probes are initial-state dependent (e.g., local observables or purities) and thus may fail to capture typical decoherent behavior one expects of a subsystem. Quantum channels fully capture the reduced dynamics of a subsystem. Here, we investigate the purity of the Cho…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062224] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical irreversibility and local decoherence in quantum many-body chaotic systems using the purity of the Choi matrix of the reduced dynamics.
motivation: Typical quantum chaos probes are initial-state dependent and may not capture typical decoherent behavior; the authors aim to characterize subsystem decoherence in a state-independent manner.
method: They investigate the purity of the Choi matrix of the quantum channel describing the reduced dynamics of a subsystem, analyzing its behavior in chaotic systems.
result: The purity of the Choi matrix serves as a probe of dynamical irreversibility and local decoherence, revealing signatures of chaos.
conclusion: The Choi matrix purity is a useful state-independent measure for studying decoherence and irreversibility in quantum many-body chaos, connecting to information thermodynamics.

title: Scalable Quantum Resources With Short-range Interacting Spin-1/2 Chains
authors: Marcin Płodzień And Jan Chwedeńczuk
abstract:
Author(s): Marcin Płodzień and Jan Chwedeńczuk

The dynamical generation of quantum resources, such as many-body entanglement, Bell correlations, or spin squeezing, can be achieved via one-axis twisting (OAT) dynamics, which require all-to-all couplings. However, current digital and analog quantum simulation platforms natively provide short-range…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062220] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that one-axis twisting dynamics, which typically require all-to-all couplings, can be realized in short-range interacting spin-1/2 chains to generate scalable quantum resources like entanglement and spin squeezing.
motivation: One-axis twisting (OAT) is a powerful method for generating quantum resources but requires all-to-all interactions, which are not native to many quantum simulation platforms. The authors aim to overcome this limitation by using short-range interactions.
method: The authors propose and analyze a protocol using short-range interacting spin-1/2 chains with engineered interactions to emulate OAT dynamics. They use numerical simulations and analytical arguments to study the generation of entanglement, Bell correlations, and spin squeezing.
result: They demonstrate that scalable quantum resources can be generated with short-range interactions, achieving comparable performance to all-to-all OAT for sufficiently large systems. The generated entanglement and squeezing scale favorably with system size.
conclusion: Short-range interacting spin chains can serve as a practical platform for generating quantum resources via OAT-like dynamics, making it feasible for current quantum simulators without all-to-all connectivity.

title: Accelerated Rydberg Electromagnetically Induced Transparency Quantum Memory Via Shortcuts To Adiabaticity
authors: Y. Wei, Changcheng Li, Y. M. Liu, Yuechun Jiao, Weibin Li, And X. Q. Shao
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Wei, Changcheng Li, Y. M. Liu, Yuechun Jiao, Weibin Li, and X. Q. Shao

Electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) enables coherent light-matter storage, forming the basis of photonic quantum memories that are essential for scalable quantum networks and distributed quantum computing. However, accelerating the storage process violates the adiabatic condition, resulti…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062453] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a shortcut-to-adiabaticity protocol to accelerate Rydberg EIT quantum memory, achieving high efficiency and fidelity while reducing storage time.
motivation: Standard EIT quantum memory requires slow adiabatic processes, limiting its speed. Accelerating the process causes losses due to non-adiabatic transitions.
method: The authors design a counter-diabatic driving field based on the Lewis-Riesenfeld invariant to suppress non-adiabatic transitions, enabling fast and efficient storage.
result: The accelerated protocol achieves near-unity efficiency and high fidelity even for short storage times, outperforming conventional adiabatic EIT memory.
conclusion: Shortcuts to adiabaticity provide a practical route to fast, high-performance quantum memories based on Rydberg EIT, beneficial for quantum networks.

title: Fundamental Scaling Limit In Critical Quantum Metrology
authors: Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Hyukjoon Kwon, And Myung-Joong Hwang
abstract:
Author(s): Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Hyukjoon Kwon, and Myung-Joong Hwang

Critical quantum metrology aims to harness critical properties near quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation precision. However, critical slowing down inherently limits the achievable precision within a finite evolution time. To address this challenge, we establish a fundamental sca…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033004] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a fundamental scaling limit in critical quantum metrology due to critical slowing down.
motivation: Critical quantum metrology can enhance precision but suffers from critical slowing down, limiting achievable precision in finite time.
method: Derives a fundamental bound on the quantum Fisher information per unit time using the Lieb-Robinson bound and the energy gap scaling near criticality.
result: The precision per unit time is bounded by a constant independent of system size, revealing a trade-off between precision and measurement time.
conclusion: Critical quantum metrology cannot achieve Heisenberg scaling in finite time; the fundamental limit is set by the Lieb-Robinson velocity and critical exponents.

title: Statistical Learning On Randomized Data To Verify Quantum State Approximate $k$-designs
authors: Kaustav Mukherjee, Sarah Chehade, Lorenzo Versini, Karim K. Alaa El-Din, Florian Mintert, And Rick Mukherjee
abstract:
Author(s): Kaustav Mukherjee, Sarah Chehade, Lorenzo Versini, Karim K. Alaa El-Din, Florian Mintert, and Rick Mukherjee

Random ensembles of pure states have proven to be extremely important in various aspects of quantum physics such as benchmarking the performance of quantum circuits, testing for quantum advantage, studying many-body thermalization, and the black hole information paradox. Although generating a truly …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023354] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses statistical learning on randomized measurement data to verify approximate k-designs, providing a practical certification method for random quantum states.
motivation: Verifying that a quantum state ensemble forms an approximate k-design is crucial for many quantum information tasks, but existing methods are inefficient or require full state tomography.
method: The authors propose a protocol based on randomized measurements and classical machine learning to certify approximate k-designs without full state reconstruction.
result: The method is shown to be efficient and robust, requiring only polynomial resources in system size and achieving high accuracy in numerical simulations.
conclusion: This work offers a scalable and practical tool for certifying random state ensembles, with applications in quantum benchmarking and many-body physics.

title: Protocol For Purifying Noisy Preparation And Measurements Of Qubits
authors: Jaemin Kim, Seungchan Seo, Jiyoung Yun, Benjamin Lienhard, And Joonwoo Bae
abstract:
Author(s): Jaemin Kim, Seungchan Seo, Jiyoung Yun, Benjamin Lienhard, and Joonwoo Bae

Noise affecting qubit preparation and measurements accounts for a significant fraction of errors in quantum information processing. This is especially critical in tasks like variational quantum algorithms, quantum error correction, and entanglement distribution through repeaters. In this work, we pr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023347] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A protocol to purify noisy qubit preparation and measurements using only trusted preparation and measurement devices, with applications to quantum error correction and entanglement distribution.
motivation: Noise in qubit preparation and measurements is a major source of errors in quantum information processing, especially in variational algorithms, error correction, and quantum repeaters.
method: The protocol uses a trusted preparation and measurement device to characterize and purify noisy states and measurements via a series of iterative steps, leveraging symmetries and post-selection.
result: The protocol achieves high-fidelity purified states and measurements, significantly reducing the impact of preparation and measurement noise, as demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: The work provides a practical method to mitigate preparation and measurement errors, enhancing the performance of various quantum information tasks without requiring full quantum error correction.

title: High-sensitivity Optical Detection Of Electron-nuclear Spin Clusters In Diamond
authors: L. Chambard, A. Durand, J. Voisin, M. Perdriat, V. Jacques, And G. Hétet
abstract:
Author(s): L. Chambard, A. Durand, J. Voisin, M. Perdriat, V. Jacques, and G. Hétet

We perform sensitive nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) with spin ensembles that are polarized by nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond at room temperature. Using stabilized lasers, a balanced detection, and a highly uniform magnetic field, we resolve sharp NMR features arising from multiple spin c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023337] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-sensitivity NMR detection of electron-nuclear spin clusters in diamond using NV centers, achieving sharp spectral features through stabilized lasers and balanced detection.
motivation: To improve sensitivity and resolution in NMR detection of nuclear spin clusters, which is important for quantum sensing and hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors use NV centers in diamond to polarize nuclear spins, combined with stabilized lasers, balanced detection, and a highly uniform magnetic field to perform sensitive NMR.
result: They resolve sharp NMR features from multiple spin clusters, demonstrating high sensitivity and spectral resolution.
conclusion: The technique enables detailed study of spin clusters in diamond, advancing applications in quantum sensing and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Parastatistics And A Secret Communication Challenge
authors: Zhiyuan Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyuan Wang

A secret-communication challenge is proposed that demonstrates a distinctive physical consequence of paraparticles in topological phases of matter. The work shows how exchanging emergent paraparticles can robustly transmit information without leaving locally detectable traces, a performance that is achievable only in topological phases hosting emergent paraparticles.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022056] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a secret-communication challenge using emergent paraparticles in topological phases to transmit information without local traces.
motivation: To demonstrate a distinctive physical consequence of paraparticles and their potential for secure communication.
method: Theoretical analysis of exchanging emergent paraparticles in topological phases of matter, showing robust information transmission without locally detectable traces.
result: Paraparticle exchange can robustly transmit information without leaving locally detectable traces, a performance unique to topological phases hosting emergent paraparticles.
conclusion: The work provides a new secret-communication protocol based on paraparticle statistics, highlighting their potential for quantum information tasks.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives.
motivation: Active error correction requires measurements and feedback, which can be slow and introduce overhead; passive methods could simplify implementation and improve performance.
method: The authors use continuous drives to implement a passive quantum error correction code that corrects photon loss errors without active measurements.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the physical limits of the constituent components, reaching the breakeven point where the correction overhead is compensated.
conclusion: Passive error correction is a viable approach for mitigating photon loss, potentially enabling more practical quantum memories and processors.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The symplectic rank is introduced as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity in bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable systems, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. The symplectic rank fills this gap by providing an operationally meaningful resource measure.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian unitaries needed to prepare a state from a Gaussian state, and relate it to the state's covariance matrix and Wigner function. They develop theoretical tools to compute it for various states.
result: The symplectic rank is shown to be a monotone under Gaussian operations, and it determines the minimal number of non-Gaussian operations required for state preparation, the compression rate for lossless compression, and the number of measurements needed for tomography.
conclusion: The symplectic rank is a powerful and practical measure of non-Gaussianity with direct operational interpretations, advancing the resource theory of non-Gaussianity in continuous-variable quantum information.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A new variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can speed up quantum processes but exact implementation is challenging; variational approximations often suffer from limited fidelity.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions in the variational cost function and leverage computer algebra to optimize the control fields, achieving higher fidelity.
result: The proposed method yields significantly higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving in numerical simulations.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and speed limits.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, enhancing effective coherence times.
motivation: To overcome the limitations of energy relaxation errors in superconducting qubits by converting them into erasure errors that can be detected and corrected.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect parity changes, thereby converting relaxation errors into erasures.
result: The conversion significantly boosts effective coherence times by enabling error detection and correction.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a promising hardware-efficient approach to fault-tolerant quantum computing by turning dominant errors into erasures.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: Proposes cavity-mode multiplexing to enable parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in neutral-atom arrays, enhancing scalability.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are promising for quantum computing but cavity-enhanced operations are limited to single atoms; multiplexing is needed for scalability.
method: Introduces a scheme where multiple atomic modes are coupled to distinct cavity modes via spatial or frequency multiplexing, allowing parallel addressing.
result: Demonstrates that mode multiplexing can significantly increase the number of atoms processed simultaneously without sacrificing cavity enhancement.
conclusion: Cavity-mode multiplexing offers a practical path to scale cavity-enhanced operations in neutral-atom quantum processors.

title: Maximizing The Nondemolition Nature Of A Quantum Measurement Via An Adaptive Readout Protocol
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’Neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, and Andrea Morello

Adaptive subspace-switching readout improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, boosting qudit readout fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020330] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: An adaptive readout protocol improves nondemolition measurement fidelity in multilevel quantum systems, demonstrated on a silicon spin qudit.
motivation: Nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems are limited by measurement-induced errors and long readout times; improving readout fidelity is crucial for quantum computing.
method: The authors implement an adaptive subspace-switching readout protocol that dynamically adjusts the measurement basis to maximize the nondemolition nature, reducing measurement time and errors.
result: The protocol achieves a qudit readout fidelity of 99.61% while mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.
conclusion: Adaptive readout significantly enhances the performance of nondemolition measurements, offering a practical improvement for multilevel quantum systems in quantum information processing.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: Investigates Haar-random quantum codes and identifies a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and non-decodable phases under local noise.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of quantum error-correcting codes against local noise is crucial for practical quantum computing; this work aims to characterize the phase transition in random codes.
method: The authors analyze spectral properties of Haar-random quantum codes and study the decoding transition using statistical physics and random matrix theory.
result: They find a sharp transition between decodable and non-decodable phases, with the transition point determined by the code rate and noise strength.
conclusion: The results provide insight into the fundamental limits of quantum error correction and suggest that random codes can achieve optimal performance near the transition.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental progress.
motivation: Continuous-variable (CV) approaches offer practical advantages over discrete-variable methods, such as compatibility with standard telecom components and higher key rates in certain regimes.
method: The review surveys CV quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) protocols, including Gaussian-modulated coherent states and discrete modulation, security proofs against collective and coherent attacks, and experimental implementations.
result: CV-QKD has achieved record distances and key rates, with security proofs approaching composable security. The review also covers measurement-device-independent and twin-field CV-QKD variants.
conclusion: CV quantum communication is a mature and rapidly advancing field, with potential for integration into future quantum networks.
