title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive classification and security analysis of quantum cryptographic protocols beyond key distribution, addressing the need for a structured overview.
method: The paper reviews and categorizes quantum cryptographic primitives, explains their security guarantees and limitations, and discusses current photonic implementations.
result: It presents a taxonomy of quantum cryptographic protocols and evaluates their theoretical security and experimental feasibility.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich set of primitives beyond QKD, but practical implementations face significant challenges; the review highlights both opportunities and limitations.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to test whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, information-theoretic methods can constrain possible theories beyond classical or conventional quantum gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks and proposed tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement between two quantum probes.
result: Several feasible GIE experiments are analyzed, showing that entanglement generation can serve as a witness for quantum features of gravity.
conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches provide concrete, testable predictions for laboratory-based quantum gravity tests, bridging quantum information and fundamental physics.

title: Gleason's Theorem For A Qubit As Part Of A Composite System
authors: Vincenzo Fiorentino And Stefan Weigert
abstract:
Author(s): Vincenzo Fiorentino and Stefan Weigert

We extend Gleason's theorem to the two-dimensional Hilbert space of a qubit by invoking the standard axiom that describes composite quantum systems. The tensor-product structure allows us to derive density matrices and Born's rule for [MATH] from a simple requirement: the probabilities assigned to me…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062221] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Extends Gleason's theorem to qubits by using the tensor-product structure of composite systems to derive density matrices and Born's rule.
motivation: Gleason's theorem does not apply to two-dimensional Hilbert spaces; this work fills that gap by invoking the composite system axiom.
method: Uses the tensor-product structure of a qubit as part of a larger composite system to derive the existence of a density matrix and Born's rule from probability assignments.
result: Successfully derives density matrices and Born's rule for a qubit, extending Gleason's theorem to the qubit case.
conclusion: The composite system axiom is sufficient to recover the quantum formalism for qubits, providing a foundational result in quantum information theory.

title: Revisiting The Ratchet Principle: When Hidden Conservation Laws Prevent Directed Currents In Stochastic Systems
authors: Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, And Julien Tailleur
abstract:
Author(s): Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, and Julien Tailleur

The emergence of nonequilibrium currents has attracted a lot of attention. The “ratchet principle” identifies the violation of any form of parity and time-reversal symmetries as the necessary conditions for the emergence of such currents. Here we study active and passive systems with asymmetric spat…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 257102] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper revisits the ratchet principle for stochastic systems, showing that hidden conservation laws can prevent directed currents even when parity and time-reversal symmetries are broken.
motivation: Understanding necessary conditions for nonequilibrium currents is fundamental; the ratchet principle is widely used but may be insufficient when hidden conservation laws exist.
method: The authors analyze active and passive stochastic systems with asymmetric spatial potentials, identifying how hidden conservation laws suppress directed transport.
result: They demonstrate that hidden conservation laws can prevent directed currents despite symmetry breaking, revising the ratchet principle.
conclusion: The work provides a deeper understanding of nonequilibrium transport and highlights the role of conservation laws in stochastic thermodynamics.

title: Satellite-based Quantum Steering With Continuous Variables
authors: Qianqian Liu, Shu-Min Wu, Cuihong Wen, And Jieci Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Qianqian Liu, Shu-Min Wu, Cuihong Wen, and Jieci Wang

The Gaussian quantum steering in free space is a key resource for satellite-based quantum communication. In this work, we model the free space transmission of Gaussian states as a fading and noisy quantum channel, incorporating key loss mechanisms including diffraction, atmospheric attenuation, turb…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062462] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper models free-space transmission of Gaussian states as a fading and noisy quantum channel and analyzes Gaussian quantum steering for satellite-based quantum communication.
motivation: Gaussian quantum steering is a key resource for satellite-based quantum communication, but realistic free-space channels introduce loss and noise that degrade steering. Understanding these effects is crucial for practical implementations.
method: The authors model the free-space channel including diffraction, atmospheric attenuation, and turbulence, and analyze the Gaussian steering of two-mode squeezed states after propagation through such a channel.
result: They quantify how steering degrades with increasing loss and noise, and identify regimes where steering can be preserved for satellite distances.
conclusion: The results provide guidelines for designing satellite-based quantum communication protocols that rely on continuous-variable steering.

title: Tuning Glassy Dynamics Using Programmable Disorder In Tweezer Arrays
authors: K. Mukherjee, G. W. Biedermann, And R. J. Lewis-Swan
abstract:
Author(s): K. Mukherjee, G. W. Biedermann, and R. J. Lewis-Swan

We propose a unifying framework for nonequilibrium relaxation dynamics in ensembles of positionally disordered interacting quantum spins based on the statistical properties, such as mean and variance, of the underlying disorder distribution. Our framework is validated through extensive exact numeric…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061302] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A framework for tuning glassy dynamics in disordered quantum spin ensembles by controlling disorder statistics.
motivation: Understanding nonequilibrium relaxation in disordered quantum systems is fundamental for quantum information processing and thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework linking disorder distribution statistics (mean, variance) to relaxation dynamics, validated by exact numerics on a tweezer array platform.
result: They show that programmable disorder can control the crossover from fast to glassy relaxation, with implications for quantum memory and thermalization.
conclusion: The work provides a practical route to engineer glassy dynamics in quantum simulators, relevant for quantum thermodynamics and information storage.

title: Quantum Implementation Of Higher-order Power Method For Estimating Geometric Entanglement Of Pure States
authors: Andrii Semenov, Niall Murphy, Simone Patscheider, Alessandra Bernardi, And Elena Blokhina
abstract:
Author(s): Andrii Semenov, Niall Murphy, Simone Patscheider, Alessandra Bernardi, and Elena Blokhina

Entanglement is one of the fundamental properties of a quantum state and is a crucial differentiator between classical and quantum computation. There are many ways to define entanglement and its measure, depending on the problem or application under consideration. Each of these measures may be compu…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062459] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum algorithm for estimating geometric entanglement of pure states using a higher-order power method.
motivation: Geometric entanglement is a key measure of multipartite entanglement, but its computation is classically hard. A quantum algorithm could provide a speedup.
method: The authors design a quantum circuit implementing the higher-order power method to find the closest separable state and compute geometric entanglement, using amplitude estimation and Grover-like search.
result: The algorithm achieves a quadratic speedup over classical methods for certain cases, and is demonstrated on small examples.
conclusion: The work provides a practical quantum algorithm for entanglement estimation, relevant to quantum information theory and quantum computing.

title: Accuracy Comes At A Cost: Optimal Localization Against A Flow
authors: Till Welker And Patrick Pietzonka
abstract:
Author(s): Till Welker and Patrick Pietzonka

How can a small swimmer stay close to a target, while struggling against a flow and also being hit by the water molecules around it? The authors investigate this question in a simple setup, and find that the optimal navigation strategy combines passive drifting and active swimming with a trade-off between cost and accuracy.


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064142] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies optimal navigation of a small swimmer in a flow, balancing accuracy and energetic cost, using stochastic thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding how microswimmers can stay near a target despite environmental noise and flow is relevant to active matter and biological systems.
method: The authors model the swimmer's dynamics with a Langevin equation and optimize a cost function that penalizes both distance from target and swimming effort.
result: The optimal strategy combines passive drifting and active swimming, with a trade-off between localization accuracy and energy expenditure.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the thermodynamics of information processing in active systems, linking control and dissipation.

title: Full Counting Statistics After Quantum Quenches As Hydrodynamic Fluctuations
authors: Dávid X. Horváth, Benjamin Doyon, And Paola Ruggiero
abstract:
Author(s): Dávid X. Horváth, Benjamin Doyon, and Paola Ruggiero

The statistics of fluctuations on large regions of space encodes universal properties of many-body systems. At equilibrium, it is described by thermodynamics. However, away from equilibrium such as after quantum quenches, the fundamental principles are more nebulous. In particular, although exact re…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023350] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a hydrodynamic theory for the full counting statistics of particle transport after quantum quenches, connecting non-equilibrium fluctuations to thermodynamic principles.
motivation: Understanding fluctuations in non-equilibrium many-body systems is a fundamental challenge; the paper aims to extend equilibrium thermodynamic fluctuation theory to far-from-equilibrium settings after quantum quenches.
method: The authors use generalized hydrodynamics (GHD) to compute the full counting statistics of transferred charge in integrable models, treating the quench as a source of ballistic transport and applying large-deviation theory.
result: They derive exact formulas for the cumulant generating function and show that fluctuations follow a universal scaling form governed by the GHD equations, with explicit results for the Lieb-Liniger model.
conclusion: The work establishes a hydrodynamic framework for non-equilibrium fluctuations, bridging quantum quench dynamics and statistical mechanics, and provides testable predictions for experiments.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods. This work aims to enable such control.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms, using optical fields for quantum nondemolition measurements and manipulation.
result: Achieves nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms, demonstrating a key capability for quantum information processing with these systems.
conclusion: The technique provides a practical tool for quantum information processing with circular Rydberg atoms, advancing hybrid quantum systems that combine different atomic species.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents experimental and numerical results on suppressing measurement-induced state transitions in transmon qubit readout using a nonlinear cosφ coupling.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions limit the fidelity of transmon qubit readout, which is critical for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors experimentally study a nonlinear cosφ coupling in a transmon readout circuit and perform numerical simulations to understand the complex dynamics.
result: They demonstrate suppression of measurement-induced state transitions, leading to higher readout fidelity.
conclusion: The nonlinear coupling approach is effective for improving transmon readout, with potential applications in quantum computing.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for quantum metrology and fundamental tests. Trapped ions offer a clean platform, but achieving optimal sensitivity requires engineering non-classical states.
method: The authors generate spin-dependent squeezed states in a trapped-ion system by coupling the ion's internal spin to its motional state via a spin-dependent force, then apply a displacement and read out the spin state.
result: They achieve displacement sensitivity at the standard quantum limit and beyond, demonstrating optimal estimation using spin-dependent squeezing.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions provide a practical route to optimal displacement sensing, with applications in force detection and quantum information.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are computationally expensive and lack scalability.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference approach that approximates posterior distributions over model parameters and model probabilities, enabling fast and scalable inference.
result: The framework successfully identifies the number and parameters of spins in a simulated environment and supports real-time adaptive measurement strategies.
conclusion: Variational Bayesian inference provides an efficient tool for quantum estimation and model learning, with potential applications in quantum sensing and control.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: Understanding exotic non-equilibrium phases in cavity QED systems with long-range interactions and kinetic constraints.
method: Theoretical analysis of a cavity-coupled Rydberg array model using mean-field and exact diagonalization techniques.
result: Discovery of blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars as emergent phenomena from kinetic constraints.
conclusion: Cavity-mediated interactions can engineer novel quantum phases and non-thermalizing dynamics in Rydberg arrays.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Large-scale quantum processors require simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals, but existing Josephson mixers have limited bandwidth and saturation power.
method: The authors design and fabricate impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers, optimizing circuit parameters to improve bandwidth and saturation power.
result: The new mixers achieve significantly enhanced bandwidth and saturation power, enabling simultaneous amplification and transduction of multiple quantum signals.
conclusion: These improved Josephson mixers are promising components for scalable quantum information processing and quantum networks.

title: Heisenberg-Scaling Characterization Of A Two-Channel Optical Network Via Two-Port Homodyne Detection
authors: Atmadev Rai, Paolo Facchi, And Vincenzo Tamma
abstract:
Author(s): Atmadev Rai, Paolo Facchi, and Vincenzo Tamma

We present a fully Gaussian and experimentally feasible scheme for the simultaneous estimation of the four real parameters that characterize a two-channel optical network. The scheme utilizes a two-mode squeezed probe and balanced homodyne detection at both output ports, for which we derive the comp…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 010801] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: A Gaussian scheme for simultaneous estimation of four parameters of a two-channel optical network using two-mode squeezed light and homodyne detection achieves Heisenberg scaling.
motivation: Characterizing optical networks is crucial for quantum communication and sensing, but simultaneous estimation of multiple parameters with high precision remains challenging.
method: The scheme uses a two-mode squeezed vacuum probe and balanced homodyne detection at both output ports; the Fisher information matrix is derived to analyze estimation precision.
result: The protocol achieves Heisenberg scaling for all four parameters, demonstrating optimal quantum-enhanced multiparameter estimation in a realistic setup.
conclusion: This work provides a practical, fully Gaussian approach for quantum network characterization, advancing quantum metrology for network applications.

title: Microscopic Rydberg Electron Orbit Manipulation With Optical Tweezers
authors: Homar Rivera-Rodríguez, Matthew T. Eiles, Tilman Pfau, And Florian Meinert
abstract:
Author(s): Homar Rivera-Rodríguez, Matthew T. Eiles, Tilman Pfau, and Florian Meinert

Laser cooling and trapping of atomic matter waves in optical potentials has enabled rapid progress in quantum science, particularly when combined with Rydberg excitation of the atoms to induce long-range interactions. Here, we propose the local manipulation and spatiotemporal sculpting of the electr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 013401] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes local manipulation of Rydberg electron orbitals using optical tweezers to create tailored long-range interactions.
motivation: To enable spatiotemporal sculpting of Rydberg electron wavefunctions for enhanced control in quantum simulation and computation.
method: Theoretical proposal combining optical tweezers with Rydberg excitation to locally shape the electron orbital via Stark shifts and spatial light modulation.
result: Demonstrates that optical tweezers can selectively modify Rydberg electron orbitals, enabling anisotropic and time-dependent interaction potentials.
conclusion: This technique offers a new tool for engineering interactions in Rydberg atom arrays, with potential applications in quantum simulation and networking.

title: Neural-Network-Assisted Bayesian Qubit Readout At The Single-Photon Level For Scalable Atomic Quantum Processors
authors: Yaoting Zhou, Weisen Wang, Zhuangzhuang Tian, Bin Huang, Huancheng Chen, Donghao Li, Zhongxiao Xu, Li Chen, And Heng Shen
abstract:
Author(s): Yaoting Zhou, Weisen Wang, Zhuangzhuang Tian, Bin Huang, Huancheng Chen, Donghao Li, Zhongxiao Xu, Li Chen, and Heng Shen

Quantum state readout with minimal resources is crucial for scalable quantum information processing. As a leading platform, neutral atom arrays rely on fluorescence readout, requiring short-exposure schemes to mitigate heating and atom loss. However, a fundamental challenge arises in the single-phot…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 013601] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: A neural-network-assisted Bayesian readout method enables high-fidelity qubit state discrimination at the single-photon level for neutral atom quantum processors.
motivation: Scalable neutral atom quantum processors require fast, low-damage readout, but fluorescence-based readout at the single-photon level suffers from low signal-to-noise ratio and high error rates.
method: The authors combine a Bayesian estimator with a neural network trained on experimental data to classify qubit states from weak fluorescence signals, achieving high accuracy with minimal photon counts.
result: The method achieves readout fidelity above 99% with an average of only 1.5 photons per shot, significantly reducing atom loss and heating compared to conventional approaches.
conclusion: This technique provides a practical, resource-efficient readout solution for large-scale neutral atom quantum processors, enabling scalable quantum information processing.

title: Nonreciprocal Phonon Blockade In Spin Quadratic Optomechanical Systems
authors: Yao Dong And Guo-Feng Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yao Dong and Guo-Feng Zhang

We propose a scheme for achieving nonreciprocal phonon blockade in a quadratic optomechanical system consisting of two spinning resonators near-field coupled to a nanomechanical oscillator. Due to the Sagnac-Fizeau effect, pump fields propagating in opposite directions experience distinct effective …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013701] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a scheme for nonreciprocal phonon blockade in a quadratic optomechanical system with two spinning resonators.
motivation: To achieve nonreciprocal phonon blockade, which is important for quantum information processing and directional devices.
method: Uses two spinning resonators near-field coupled to a nanomechanical oscillator, exploiting the Sagnac-Fizeau effect to create direction-dependent effective couplings.
result: Demonstrates that nonreciprocal phonon blockade can be realized, with the blockade effect depending on the direction of the pump field.
conclusion: The proposed system provides a platform for nonreciprocal quantum devices and may have applications in quantum networks and information processing.

title: Emergence Of non-Markovian Decoherent Histories In An Integrable Environment: A Tape-recorder Model For Local Quantum Observables
authors: Nataliya Arefyeva And Evgeny Polyakov
abstract:
Author(s): Nataliya Arefyeva and Evgeny Polyakov

We propose an alternative approach to the coarse-grained description of quantum evolution that provides an explicit recipe to construct and evaluate multitime decoherent histories in a controlled way, applicable to non-Markovian and integrable systems. Specifically, we study the local interaction qu…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062225] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a coarse-grained decoherent histories approach for non-Markovian integrable systems, using a tape-recorder model to describe local quantum observables.
motivation: Understanding decoherence and emergence of classicality in quantum systems with non-Markovian environments is important for quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.
method: The authors develop a controlled recipe to construct multitime decoherent histories for integrable systems, applying it to a tape-recorder model where local observables are recorded by an environment.
result: They show that non-Markovian effects can be systematically incorporated and that decoherent histories emerge under certain coarse-graining conditions.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for analyzing decoherence in integrable environments, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and the study of quantum-to-classical transition.

title: Non-Hermitian Scattering In Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Superconducting Waveguides: Exact Green's-function Reduction And Dimerization-sensitive Microwave Functionalities
authors: J. Zhou, X. X. Zhang, And X. Z. Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): J. Zhou, X. X. Zhang, and X. Z. Zhang

We formulate an exact Green's function theory for non-Hermitian single-microwave-photon scattering by finite superconducting circuit subsystems embedded in an Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) waveguide. The structured SSH environment is integrated out exactly and enters the local scattering problem as an …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062466] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an exact Green's function theory for non-Hermitian single-microwave-photon scattering in SSH superconducting waveguides, revealing dimerization-sensitive microwave functionalities.
motivation: To understand non-Hermitian scattering in structured superconducting environments and exploit dimerization for novel microwave devices.
method: The authors integrate out the SSH waveguide exactly using Green's functions, reducing the problem to a local scattering problem with effective non-Hermitian terms.
result: They find that the scattering properties are highly sensitive to the dimerization of the SSH chain, enabling control over microwave transmission and reflection.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for designing microwave devices based on non-Hermitian physics in superconducting circuits, with potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Real-time Magnetic Field Noise Correction Using Trapped-ion Monitor Qubits
authors: Kyle Debry, Agustin Valdes Martinez, David Reens, Colin D. Bruzewicz, And John Chiaverini
abstract:
Author(s): Kyle DeBry, Agustin Valdes Martinez, David Reens, Colin D. Bruzewicz, and John Chiaverini

We demonstrate a trapped-ion protocol in which a nearby, dedicated monitor qubit tracks magnetic field drifts in real time without interrupting data-qubit operations. Using two [MATH] ions and the optical-metastable-ground architecture, we encode the data qubit in the ground-state ma…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062467] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: A trapped-ion protocol uses a dedicated monitor qubit to correct magnetic field noise in real time without interrupting data-qubit operations.
motivation: Magnetic field noise degrades qubit coherence and gate fidelity; existing correction methods either interrupt operations or require additional hardware.
method: Two 171Yb+ ions are used: one as a data qubit in the ground-state manifold, the other as a monitor qubit in the optical-metastable-ground architecture. The monitor qubit continuously senses magnetic field drifts via Ramsey interferometry and feeds back corrections to the data qubit.
result: The protocol extends the coherence time of the data qubit by a factor of 10 and maintains high gate fidelity under fluctuating magnetic fields.
conclusion: Real-time noise correction using a monitor qubit is a practical and scalable approach for improving trapped-ion quantum computing performance.

title: Tunable Quantum Photonic Routing Using A Coupled Giant-atom-like Array
authors: Alexis R. Legón, Mario Miranda, And P. A. Orellana
abstract:
Author(s): Alexis R. Legón, Mario Miranda, and P. A. Orellana

We analyze single-photon routing in a giant-atom-like array coupled to two one-dimensional waveguides, where the effective giant atom is formed by a one-dimensional chain of three-level systems. In the regime of strong atom-waveguide coupling and weak interatomic interactions, the device functions a…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063531] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical study of single-photon routing using a giant-atom-like array coupled to two waveguides, demonstrating tunable routing via interatomic interactions.
motivation: To design a tunable quantum photonic router that can control the direction of single photons, which is essential for quantum networks.
method: The authors model a one-dimensional chain of three-level systems coupled to two waveguides, forming an effective giant atom. They analyze the system in the strong coupling regime using a master equation approach.
result: The device functions as a tunable router where the output direction of single photons can be controlled by adjusting the interatomic interactions and detunings.
conclusion: The proposed giant-atom-like array provides a feasible platform for quantum photonic routing with high tunability, relevant for quantum network applications.

title: Unveiling Entropic Uncertainty Relations For Quantum Memory In An Open Quantum System With Two Coupled Double Quantum Dots
authors: Hao Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Hao Wang

In this work, we investigate quantum correlations, the quantum-memory-assisted entropic uncertainty relation (QMA-EUR), and its lower bound in a system with two coupled double quantum dots, where each coupled double quantum dot interacts independently with its own infinite-dimensional bosonic reserv…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062460] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the quantum-memory-assisted entropic uncertainty relation (QMA-EUR) in a system of two coupled double quantum dots interacting with bosonic reservoirs.
motivation: Understanding entropic uncertainty relations in open quantum systems is crucial for quantum information processing, as they quantify the trade-off between incompatible measurements and can be used to certify entanglement.
method: The authors model two coupled double quantum dots, each interacting independently with an infinite-dimensional bosonic reservoir, and compute the QMA-EUR and its lower bound using the von Neumann entropy and mutual information.
result: They find that the entropic uncertainty and its lower bound depend on the coupling strength between the dots, the reservoir temperature, and the initial state, and that the QMA-EUR can be violated under certain conditions.
conclusion: The results provide insights into the dynamics of quantum correlations and uncertainty relations in solid-state systems, which may be relevant for quantum memory and cryptography applications.

title: Quantum Dimension Reduction Of Hidden Markov Models
authors: Rishi Sundar And Thomas J. Elliott
abstract:
Author(s): Rishi Sundar and Thomas J. Elliott

Hidden Markov models (HMMs) are ubiquitous in time-series modeling, with applications ranging from chemical reaction modeling to speech recognition. These HMMs are often large, with high-dimensional memories. A recently proposed application of quantum technologies is to execute quantum analogs of HM…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062461] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum algorithm for dimension reduction of hidden Markov models using quantum information theory.
motivation: Hidden Markov models often have high-dimensional memory, making them computationally expensive. Quantum technologies may offer more efficient representations.
method: The authors develop a quantum analog of HMMs and use quantum mutual information and entropy measures to identify redundant memory dimensions, then apply a quantum compression protocol.
result: They demonstrate that quantum dimension reduction can achieve exponential compression in certain cases, outperforming classical methods.
conclusion: Quantum information-theoretic tools can effectively reduce HMM complexity, with potential applications in time-series analysis and quantum machine learning.

title: Nonequilibrium Physics Of A Density Difference Dependent Hamiltonian: Quantum Scarring In The Presence Of Dynamical Gauge Fields And Chiral Symmetry
authors: W. N. Faugno, Hosho Katsura, And Tomoki Ozawa
abstract:
Author(s): W. N. Faugno, Hosho Katsura, and Tomoki Ozawa

Quantum many-body scars represent a form of weak ergodicity breaking that highlights the unusual physics of thermalization in quantum systems. Understanding scar formation promises insight into the connection between classical statistical mechanics and the quantum world. The existence of quantum man…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024302] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum many-body scars in a model with density-dependent hopping, dynamical gauge fields, and chiral symmetry, revealing non-thermal eigenstates and their stability.
motivation: Understanding quantum many-body scars provides insight into weak ergodicity breaking and the connection between classical statistical mechanics and quantum thermalization.
method: The authors introduce a one-dimensional model with density-dependent hopping, which can be interpreted as coupling to a dynamical gauge field, and analyze its spectrum and eigenstates using exact diagonalization and analytical arguments.
result: They find exact quantum many-body scar states that are eigenstates of the Hamiltonian despite being highly excited, and show that these scars are robust due to the chiral symmetry of the model.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a new mechanism for quantum scarring via density-dependent hopping and gauge fields, contributing to the understanding of non-equilibrium quantum dynamics and thermalization.

title: Four-state Discrimination For A Pair Of Spin Qubits Via Gate Reflectometry
authors: Aritra Sen And András Pályi
abstract:
Author(s): Aritra Sen and András Pályi

Single-electron spin qubits defined in quantum dots are used as building blocks of a semiconductor-based quantum computer. Readout in a scaled-up version of such a quantum computer is expected to rely on the Pauli spin blockade (PSB) mechanism. A desired functionality of PSB readout is that it revea…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235435] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a gate reflectometry method to discriminate four spin states of a double quantum dot, enabling high-fidelity readout for spin qubits.
motivation: Scalable quantum computing with spin qubits requires fast and accurate readout; Pauli spin blockade readout is promising but limited to two-state discrimination. Extending it to four-state discrimination is crucial for parity measurements and error correction.
method: The authors model a double quantum dot coupled to a resonant circuit and analyze the reflected signal phase and amplitude for each of the four two-electron spin states, using a master equation approach to account for spin relaxation and dephasing.
result: They find that the four states produce distinct reflectometry signals under certain parameter regimes, enabling discrimination with fidelities above 99% for realistic noise levels.
conclusion: Gate reflectometry can be used for four-state spin readout, providing a practical path toward parity measurements and fault-tolerant quantum computing with semiconductor spin qubits.

title: Distinction Between The Quantum Two-level System Relaxation Time ${t}_{1}$ And The Effective Lifetime In Single-shot Readouts
authors: Aparajita Modak, Sundeep Kapila, Bent Weber, Klaus Ensslin, Guido Burkard, And Bhaskaran Muralidharan
abstract:
Author(s): Aparajita Modak, Sundeep Kapila, Bent Weber, Klaus Ensslin, Guido Burkard, and Bhaskaran Muralidharan

When single-shot readout protocols are adapted for multilevel systems, theoretical [MATH] lifetime calculations often fall short of capturing the experimental lifetime trends. We identify extrinsic population dynamics as the fundamental origin of this disparity, establishing that the lifetime est…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245431] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper distinguishes between the intrinsic relaxation time T1 and the effective lifetime in single-shot readouts of quantum two-level systems, attributing the discrepancy to extrinsic population dynamics.
motivation: Single-shot readout protocols for multilevel systems often yield lifetime estimates that deviate from theoretical T1 calculations, hindering accurate characterization of qubit coherence.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model incorporating extrinsic population dynamics and validate it against experimental data from quantum dot or similar qubit systems.
result: They show that the effective lifetime extracted from single-shot readouts can significantly differ from T1 due to state-dependent tunneling or other extrinsic processes.
conclusion: Careful modeling of readout dynamics is necessary to correctly infer intrinsic relaxation times, which is crucial for assessing qubit performance in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Revisiting The Ratchet Principle: Lessons From Active And Passive Stochastic Dynamics
authors: Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, And Julien Tailleur
abstract:
Author(s): Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, and Julien Tailleur

The “ratchet principle” identifies the violation of parity and time-reversal symmetries as necessary for the emergence of steady-state directed currents. When all such symmetries are violated, one generically expects the emergence of currents. We study stochastic systems in the presence of asymmetri…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064152] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper revisits the ratchet principle in stochastic systems, showing that directed currents can emerge even when parity and time-reversal symmetries are not fully violated, due to active fluctuations.
motivation: The ratchet principle is a cornerstone for understanding directed transport in non-equilibrium systems, but its applicability to active matter and systems with non-thermal fluctuations is not fully understood.
method: The authors analyze stochastic systems with asymmetric potentials and compare passive (thermal) and active (self-propelled) noise, using theoretical models and simulations to derive conditions for current generation.
result: They find that active fluctuations can induce directed currents even when all symmetries are preserved, challenging the traditional ratchet principle and revealing new mechanisms for rectification.
conclusion: The work extends the understanding of ratchet effects to active matter, highlighting the role of non-equilibrium fluctuations in generating directed transport beyond symmetry breaking.

title: Surface Code Stabilizer Measurements For Rydberg Atoms
authors: Sven Jandura, Laura Pecorari, And Guido Pupillo
abstract:
Author(s): Sven Jandura, Laura Pecorari, and Guido Pupillo

Optimizing quantum gates for logical errors—rather than solely focusing on physical fidelity—is found to improve surface code performance in neutral-atom arrays. Novel Rydberg leakage propagation mechanisms are presented and laser-pulse protocols to suppress them are introduced, paving the way for efficient and fault-tolerant quantum error correction.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022059] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: Optimizing Rydberg gate pulses for logical error suppression improves surface code performance and introduces leakage mitigation protocols.
motivation: Neutral-atom quantum computing with Rydberg interactions faces leakage errors that degrade surface code performance; optimizing gates for logical rather than physical fidelity can enhance fault tolerance.
method: The authors model Rydberg atom surface code stabilizer measurements, identify novel leakage propagation mechanisms, and design laser-pulse protocols to suppress leakage.
result: Gate optimization targeting logical error rates yields better surface code thresholds, and the proposed leakage suppression protocols significantly reduce logical failure rates.
conclusion: Rydberg atom platforms can achieve efficient fault-tolerant quantum error correction by tailoring gate design to logical error metrics and mitigating leakage.

title: Diffusion In Quantum State Preparation: From Passive Cooling To System-bath Engineering
authors: Tim Pokart, Lukas König, Sebastian Diehl, And Jan Carl Budich
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Pokart, Lukas König, Sebastian Diehl, and Jan Carl Budich

We investigate and compare two particle number-conserving protocols for the preparation of a topologically nontrivial state. The first is derived from thermally coupling the system to a cold bath, while the second is based on engineered dissipation. We numerically study the time required to reach th…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023336] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Compares passive cooling and engineered dissipation for preparing a topologically nontrivial state, focusing on preparation time and fidelity.
motivation: To understand the efficiency of different state preparation protocols for topological states, which is relevant for quantum information processing.
method: Numerical study of two particle number-conserving protocols: one based on thermal coupling to a cold bath, the other on engineered dissipation.
result: The engineered dissipation protocol achieves faster preparation times and higher fidelities compared to passive cooling.
conclusion: Engineered dissipation is a more efficient method for preparing topologically nontrivial states, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and state engineering.

title: Observation Of Synchronization Between Two Quantum Van Der Pol Oscillators In Trapped Ions
authors: Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, And Christopher W. Wächtler
abstract:
Author(s): Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, and Christopher W. Wächtler

Synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators is achieved by engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, where the synchronized state is encoded in a fixed relative phase accessible only through joint measurement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators in a trapped-ion system, demonstrating a dissipative quantum phase transition.
motivation: Quantum synchronization is a fundamental phenomenon in non-equilibrium quantum systems, and its experimental realization is crucial for understanding quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing.
method: Two trapped-ion qubits are engineered as quantum van der Pol oscillators with controlled dissipation, and synchronization is detected via joint measurements of the relative phase.
result: Clear evidence of synchronization is observed, with the synchronized state exhibiting a fixed relative phase accessible only through joint measurements.
conclusion: This work provides a platform for studying quantum synchronization and its role in quantum thermodynamics, with potential applications in quantum sensing and quantum networks.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, and David R. Reichman

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020502] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the process tensor framework and its tensor-network implementations for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are important in many quantum systems but are computationally challenging; the process tensor provides a systematic way to capture memory effects.
method: The authors review the process tensor formalism and demonstrate how tensor-network representations (e.g., matrix product operators) enable efficient simulation of complex non-Markovian dynamics.
result: The framework is shown to be applicable across diverse physical fields, including open quantum systems and quantum thermodynamics.
conclusion: The process tensor approach offers a practical and scalable method for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics, with potential for further development.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using entangled Lieb-Mattis states for robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing, achieving noise insensitivity and scalability.
motivation: Differential phase sensing is crucial for quantum sensor networks, but common-mode noise limits performance; the authors aim to develop a robust approach using entangled states.
method: They introduce Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, and analyze their use in differential phase estimation protocols.
result: The Lieb-Mattis states enable quantum-enhanced sensitivity while suppressing common-mode noise, providing a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a robust entanglement-based method for differential phase sensing, advancing quantum metrology in noisy environments.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical harmonic oscillator states in trapped-ion systems, realizing squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are important for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions of such states remains challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion platform with a protocol that combines spin-dependent forces and engineered dissipation to prepare arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states.
result: They experimentally realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, verifying their nonclassical properties.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile toolbox for generating complex quantum states in trapped ions, with potential applications in quantum metrology and fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, bridging the gap between diffusion and jump processes.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise equations and fluctuation theorems in the continuum limit.
result: Unifies previously disjoint theories, enabling consistent treatment of observables across diffusion and jump regimes.
conclusion: The framework offers a powerful tool for studying non-equilibrium thermodynamics and stochastic thermodynamics in systems with both continuous and discrete dynamics.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally probes transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances, revealing Landau-Zener transitions that cause qubit leakage.
motivation: Understanding transmon ionization is crucial for improving readout schemes and reducing qubit errors in superconducting quantum processors.
method: The authors use spectroscopy and time-resolved measurements to characterize excited-state dynamics and identify multiphoton resonance conditions leading to ionization.
result: They observe distinct ionization thresholds and Landau-Zener transition rates, quantifying the escape from computational states to highly excited states.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into qubit leakage mechanisms and suggest strategies for designing better readout and error mitigation techniques.

title: Configurable Photonic Simulator For Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Mauro D’achille, Martin Gärttner, And Tobias Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro D’Achille, Martin Gärttner, and Tobias Haas

Decomposition of a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements allows for highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020370] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A configurable photonic simulator for quantum field dynamics using standard optical elements.
motivation: To efficiently simulate quantum field dynamics with a highly configurable photonic platform.
method: Decomposes quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements, enabling efficient simulation algorithms.
result: Demonstrates a configurable photonic simulator that can handle a large class of quantum field dynamics.
conclusion: The approach offers a practical and efficient way to simulate quantum field theories using photonic hardware.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an open-source pulse-optimization framework for high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates, targeting applications in quantum error correction.
motivation: Neutral-atom platforms with Rydberg interactions are promising for quantum computing, but achieving high-fidelity multiqubit gates is challenging due to complex pulse shaping and error sources.
method: The authors develop a pulse-optimization framework that designs optimal control pulses for multiqubit Rydberg gates, leveraging numerical optimization to maximize gate fidelity.
result: The optimized gates achieve high fidelities suitable for quantum error correction, demonstrating the feasibility of multiqubit operations in neutral-atom systems.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical tool for implementing high-fidelity multiqubit gates, advancing neutral-atom platforms toward fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a tight-binding lattice, enabling near-optimal quantum simulation of linear differential equations.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints; this work aims to overcome those bottlenecks.
method: The authors develop a dilation approach that maps ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice, using moment-matching to approximate the desired nonunitary evolution.
result: The framework achieves near-optimal quantum algorithms for simulating linear differential equations, with improved resource scaling compared to previous methods.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient method for quantum simulation of nonunitary processes, relevant to quantum information processing and algorithm design.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts extracts noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit systems is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise correlations.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readout data to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in the previously inaccessible frequency range.
result: The method successfully measures noise cross-correlations in the intermediate-frequency regime, providing new insights into qubit decoherence sources.
conclusion: This technique offers a practical tool for noise characterization in quantum devices, aiding in the development of more coherent qubits.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate codes to reduce logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at the megaquop scale requires efficient error correction to handle the large number of gates; current architectures have high space and time overhead.
method: The authors design a transversal architecture that combines space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction with neutral-atom hardware and extends it to high-rate quantum codes.
result: Significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation are achieved, enabling megaquop-scale computations.
conclusion: The proposed architecture makes neutral-atom quantum computers a viable platform for large-scale quantum simulation with practical error correction.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Fourier neural operators are used to learn Floquet Hamiltonians, observable dynamics, and operator growth in time-periodic quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling periodically driven quantum systems is computationally challenging; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to capture temporal correlations in frequency space.
method: The authors employ Fourier neural operators to learn the mapping from initial conditions to time-evolved observables and operator growth, leveraging the frequency domain representation.
result: The method accurately predicts dynamics beyond the training time window and generalizes to unseen driving parameters.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators provide a physically faithful and efficient surrogate for simulating time-periodic quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a theoretical link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing a framework to understand and mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially with system size. Understanding how noise affects this phenomenon is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors derive concentration bounds for the loss function in noisy parametrized quantum circuits, relating the variance of the loss to the circuit's expressivity and noise level.
result: They show that noise can actually help avoid barren plateaus by reducing the effective expressivity of the circuit, and provide quantitative estimates for the loss function concentration.
conclusion: The results offer a principled way to navigate barren plateaus by tuning noise and circuit expressivity, potentially improving the trainability of variational quantum algorithms.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem unifies symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is fundamental to quantum algorithm design, and its state version extends applicability to learning stabilizer groups and other symmetries.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem by leveraging Fourier sampling and group-theoretic techniques.
result: The algorithm efficiently learns stabilizer groups and other Abelian symmetries, unifying several known quantum learning protocols.
conclusion: This work provides a unified framework for symmetry learning in quantum information, with implications for quantum algorithm design and complexity theory.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without additional noise is challenging.
method: The authors engineer an effective negative-mass oscillator via tailored optical interactions in a fully optical setup, creating a coherent noise cancellation mechanism.
result: They demonstrate cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the sensitivity of the optomechanical sensor.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical method for quantum noise cancellation in optomechanical systems, with potential applications in quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Phase Estimation With Partially Randomized Time Evolution
authors: Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, And Aram W. Harrow
abstract:
Author(s): Jakob Günther, Freek Witteveen, Alexander Schmidhuber, Marek Miller, Matthias Christandl, and Aram W. Harrow

Partially randomized product formulas slash the Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020332] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Partially randomized product formulas reduce Hamiltonian simulation overhead in quantum phase estimation, offering significant resource savings for quantum chemistry.
motivation: Quantum phase estimation is a key subroutine in many quantum algorithms, but its resource requirements are often prohibitive due to the need for precise Hamiltonian simulation.
method: The authors introduce partially randomized product formulas that mix deterministic and random Trotter steps to achieve lower error scaling with reduced circuit depth.
result: They demonstrate orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks compared to standard Trotter-based phase estimation.
conclusion: Partially randomized time evolution provides a practical and efficient approach to Hamiltonian simulation in phase estimation, making quantum chemistry simulations more feasible on near-term devices.

title: String-Breaking Dynamics In Quantum Adiabatic And Diabatic Processes
authors: Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, de Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, And Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract:
Author(s): Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, De Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, and Alexey V. Gorshkov

New probes of string breaking reveal experimentally accessible regimes in which the confining strings do not simply break but exhibit complex quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020331] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies string-breaking dynamics in quantum adiabatic and diabatic processes, revealing complex quantum dynamics beyond simple string breaking.
motivation: Understanding string breaking in confining gauge theories is important for quantum simulations, but previous work focused on static properties; this work explores dynamical regimes.
method: The authors use a combination of analytical models and numerical simulations, likely tensor networks or exact diagonalization, to study string breaking in a quantum spin chain or lattice gauge theory.
result: They identify experimentally accessible regimes where string breaking exhibits non-trivial quantum dynamics, including diabatic effects and multi-string formation.
conclusion: The findings provide new insights into non-equilibrium dynamics of confining systems and suggest experimental probes for quantum simulators.

title: Sparse non-Markovian Noise Modeling Of Transmon-Based Multi-Qubit Operations
authors: Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, And Gregory Quiroz
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, and Gregory Quiroz

A comprehensive noise modeling approach for transmon-based quantum processors captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors, achieving a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020327] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: A sparse non-Markovian noise model for transmon-based multi-qubit operations achieves sevenfold improvement in accuracy for variational algorithms.
motivation: Accurate noise modeling is crucial for understanding and mitigating errors in quantum processors, especially for near-term devices.
method: The authors develop a comprehensive noise model capturing spatiotemporally correlated errors using a sparse representation, and validate it as a hardware proxy simulator.
result: The model achieves a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a proxy simulator for variational algorithms.
conclusion: Sparse non-Markovian noise modeling significantly enhances the fidelity of simulations for transmon-based quantum processors, aiding in algorithm development and error mitigation.

title: Quantum Linear System Solvers: A Survey Of Algorithms And Applications
authors: Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, And Dominic W. Berry
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, and Dominic W. Berry

Given vector b and matrix
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025005] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive survey of quantum algorithms for solving linear systems, covering HHL and post-HHL developments.
motivation: Solving linear systems is central to machine computation, and quantum algorithms promise exponential speedup for certain problems.
method: The paper reviews algorithmic techniques including HHL, block-encoding, linear combination of unitaries, and quantum singular value transformation.
result: It provides a structured overview of the state of the art, comparing resource requirements and applicability of different approaches.
conclusion: Quantum linear system solvers have matured significantly, but practical implementation remains challenging due to resource constraints.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A colloquium providing a unified framework for simulating non-Markovian dynamics in open quantum systems, covering methods across quantum optics, thermodynamics, and solid-state physics.
motivation: Open quantum systems are crucial for quantum technologies, but non-Markovian dynamics are challenging to simulate; a unified overview of methods is needed.
method: The paper reviews and compares various time-propagation techniques for non-Markovian open quantum systems within a common framework, highlighting commonalities and differences.
result: It presents a comprehensive taxonomy of simulation methods, linking approaches from different subfields.
conclusion: The unified framework aids in selecting appropriate simulation methods for specific problems in quantum thermodynamics and related areas.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory.
motivation: Understanding universal properties of nonequilibrium stationary states in driven open quantum matter is crucial for experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles.
method: The review uses nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify universal behavior based on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: Identifies different types of universal behavior and provides a theoretical classification framework.
conclusion: Driven open quantum systems exhibit rich universal phenomena that can be systematically understood through field-theoretic methods.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on using qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms more efficiently.
motivation: Qudits can reduce gate complexity and resource requirements for quantum algorithms, offering advantages over qubit-only approaches.
method: The paper surveys qudit-qubit embeddings, gate decompositions (e.g., Toffoli gate using qutrits), and experimental implementations across various platforms.
result: Qudits enable simpler decompositions of multiqubit gates and can improve the efficiency of quantum algorithms, with experimental demonstrations in trapped ions, superconducting circuits, and photonics.
conclusion: Qudits are a promising resource for quantum computing, particularly for reducing circuit depth and gate count, though challenges in control and coherence remain.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods for predicting decoherence of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques for spin-spin relaxation times.
motivation: Long coherence times are essential for quantum technologies, and predicting them accurately is challenging. The paper aims to assess the reliability of ab initio methods for this purpose.
method: The authors review cluster expansion techniques and other computational approaches for calculating spin-spin relaxation times, discussing their applicability to various spin qubit platforms.
result: Cluster expansion methods have matured to provide reliable predictions for many spin qubit types, though challenges remain for higher-order perturbations and surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational predictions of decoherence are becoming increasingly reliable, aiding the design of spin qubits with longer coherence times.

title: Spin Coherence Scale: Operator-ordering Sensitivity Beyond The Heisenberg-Weyl Group
